from solution import same_order


def test_issue_example_from_description():
    """Example from issue returns True when common order matches."""
    # common l1 order has 3 items, l2 order has 3 items, 3 == 3 and equal -> True
    assert same_order(["red", "green", "black", "orange"], ["red", "pink", "green", "white", "black"]) == True


def test_issue_identical_lists_same_order():
    """Identical lists have common elements in the same order."""
    # common count 3 == 3 and positions equal -> True
    assert same_order(["a", "b", "c"], ["a", "b", "c"]) == True


def test_issue_interspersed_uncommon_still_true():
    """Common elements in same order with different uncommon items returns True."""
    # common l1 has 3 items, common l2 has 3 items, 3 == 3 and equal -> True
    assert same_order(["a", "x", "b", "y", "c"], ["a", "z", "b", "z", "c"]) == True


def test_issue_minimal_swapped_pair_is_false():
    """Swapped pair of common elements is not in the same order."""
    # common count 2 == 2 but 1 + 1 positions differ -> False
    assert same_order(["a", "b"], ["b", "a"]) == False


def test_issue_reversed_three_is_false():
    """Reversed order of three common elements returns False."""
    # common count 3 == 3 but order differs in 3 - 1 = 2 places -> False
    assert same_order(["red", "green", "black"], ["black", "green", "red"]) == False


def test_issue_partial_misorder_is_false():
    """Three commons with last two swapped returns False."""
    # common count 3 == 3 but last 2 of 3 swapped -> False
    assert same_order(["a", "b", "c", "d"], ["a", "c", "b", "d"]) == False


def test_issue_single_common_is_true():
    """A single common element is trivially in the same order."""
    # common count 1 == 1 so order holds -> True
    assert same_order(["a", "b", "c"], ["x", "y", "b", "z"]) == True


def test_issue_no_common_is_true():
    """Lists with no common elements are vacuously in the same order."""
    # common count 0 == 0 so empty orders match -> True
    assert same_order(["a", "b"], ["c", "d"]) == True


def test_issue_both_empty_is_true():
    """Two empty lists have no common elements so are in the same order."""
    # common count 0 == 0 so 0 + 0 = 0 items match -> True
    assert same_order([], []) == True


def test_contract_takes_two_list_arguments():
    """same_order(l1, l2) is callable with two list arguments."""
    # common count 1 == 1 so 1 - 0 = 1 match -> True
    assert same_order(["a"], ["a"]) == True


def test_contract_integer_lists_supported():
    """Two given lists may hold integers and still compare common order."""
    # common count 3 == 3 and order equal, 2 + 1 = 3 items -> True
    assert same_order([1, 2, 3, 4], [1, 9, 2, 8, 3]) == True
